title: SK Launches First Impact Booster Cohort to Collaborate with Social Ventures
summary: Terracle was selected as one of nine companies in the first SK Impact Booster cohort.
It plans to develop collaboration models for carbon reduction and circularity through technical demonstrations and business partnerships with SK affiliates.
caption: 2026 SK임팩트부스터 1기 오리엔테이션 / 행복나래 제공

body.text: Happynarae, a social enterprise established by SK, confirmed nine companies for the inaugural SK Impact Booster program and announced the start of business partnerships and growth support with SK affiliates. Terracle was selected in recognition of its environmental and energy technologies and potential for business collaboration.
A scale-up program for growing social ventures

SK Impact Booster is an impact startup scale-up program led by the SV Committee of SK SUPEX Council and jointly operated by Happynarae. It identifies social ventures pursuing both solutions to social problems and business growth, offering practical collaboration opportunities with SK affiliates and business support funding.

Selected companies receive KRW 10 million in business support. Those undertaking proof-of-concept projects with SK affiliates may receive up to an additional KRW 60 million. Further support includes expert mentoring, legal and public relations assistance and connections to fundraising opportunities.
Nine companies selected from more than 300 applicants

More than 300 social ventures applied. SK selected the final nine after three rounds—expert document review, evaluation by working-level departments of SK affiliates, and interviews—assessing growth potential and collaboration synergies.

The nine companies are Deeping Source, Starstech, Aim Intelligence, Ents, NT, Oldowan, JeClean, Terracle and FirstLab. They work across environmental and energy solutions, industrial safety and security, artificial intelligence and other technology-led social innovation fields.
Terracle to develop carbon reduction and circularity partnerships

SK plans to align the business needs of its affiliates with the selected companies' technologies, developing collaborations in safe AI adoption, carbon reduction, circularity, removal of hazardous industrial substances and workplace safety.

Terracle will explore business partnerships and technology demonstrations with SK affiliates using its chemical recycling technology, which returns waste plastics to their original feedstocks. The company plans to use this selection to extend the field applications of circularity technology and achieve measurable carbon reductions with industrial partners.

Happynarae said it would continue offering practical support—including cooperation with SK affiliates and financial backing—to help social ventures at a key point in their growth reach the next stage.

title: Terracle and the Korean Army Partner to Recycle Waste Textiles
summary: Advanced environmental technology helps reduce waste textiles generated by military bases.
The partnership supports circularity in the public sector, resource security and reduced plastic dependence.
caption: 테라클이 육군5군수지원사령부와 ‘폐섬유 재활용을 위한 상호협력 업무협약(MOU)’을 체결했다. 좌측 5군지사 박준범 사령관, 우측 테라클 권기백 대표이사 / 테라클 제공

body.text: [Today Energy, reporter Kim Byeong-min] Terracle, which chemically recycles waste PET plastics and textiles through depolymerization, announced that it signed an MOU with the Republic of Korea Army's 5th Logistics Support Command on May 26 for cooperation on textile waste recycling. Rather than simply disposing of or incinerating waste textiles generated by the military, the partnership aims to recover high-purity recycled feedstocks through depolymerization.

The 5th Logistics Support Command is a key rear-area military logistics unit responsible for supply, maintenance and transport. Supporting numerous military units also results in substantial volumes of discarded bedding, mattresses, uniforms and other textiles.

Through proactive public administration, the command initiated cooperation with an advanced private-sector environmental technology provider. The agreement is expected to establish a model for reducing waste disposal costs while contributing to national carbon neutrality and circularity efforts.

Terracle operates depolymerization technology that breaks waste plastics and polyester-based textiles down at the molecular level, recovering raw petrochemical materials such as terephthalic acid (TPA) and ethylene glycol (EG). This next-generation approach addresses limitations of mechanical recycling. The company was selected as a preliminary Green Unicorn startup by Korea's climate and environment authorities in 2025.

Terracle recently completed what it describes as Korea's first hydrolysis depolymerization plant with annual recycling capacity of 4,000 tons. Ahead of full commercial operations, it is preparing to process large volumes of military waste in the second half of the year, contributing to greenhouse-gas reduction and carbon-neutrality targets.

The Korean government is pursuing policies to replace virgin materials with recycled feedstocks derived from waste and gradually expand mandatory recycled-content requirements. With geopolitical risks increasing instability in petroleum supply chains, feedstock recovery from waste is also regarded as strategically important for national resource security.

Unlike one-off waste collection campaigns, this agreement establishes an ongoing collaboration designed to convert large-scale military waste into recycled feedstocks that can be used in real industrial production.

Terracle CEO Kwon Kibaek said the 5th Logistics Support Command's proactive establishment of a circularity system was a landmark for expanding circularity in the public sector. He added that the company intends to extend cooperation to other public institutions facing large volumes of discarded uniforms and textiles, in line with government recycled-content and plastic-reduction policies.

Founded in 2021, Terracle chemically recycles waste PET plastics and textiles into TPA and EG for sale. Its core technology is hydrolysis depolymerization. The company has completed its first commercial plant in Dangjin, Chungcheongnam-do and has raised a cumulative KRW 15.9 billion from investors including Hyundai Motor, DSC Investment and Envisioning Partners.
Terminology
Depolymerization is a technology that uses chemical or thermal processes to break down macromolecules such as plastics and polymers into their original raw materials or monomer components.

title: Turning Hard-to-Recycle Marine Plastics into Raw Materials: Terracle Earns ISCC PLUS OBP Verification
summary: Depolymerization technology overcomes the limits of conventional recycling.
Terracle presents a new model for marine waste circularity.
caption: 해양 부유 폐기물 수거 현장 / 테라클 제공

body.text: Terracle, a chemical recycling company led by CEO Kwon Kibaek, received international recognition for technology that converts discarded marine waste into chemical feedstocks comparable to virgin petrochemical raw materials. Obtaining Ocean-Bound Plastic (OBP) recognition under ISCC PLUS provides an important qualification for joining global sustainable materials supply chains.

ISCC PLUS is an international sustainability verification system widely used in chemical, textile and packaging industries worldwide, particularly in Europe. Global brands use it to verify recycled feedstocks, track materials from origin through processing to final products, and support ESG reporting with reliable evidence.

The certification specifically includes Ocean-Bound Plastic (OBP): waste plastics generated within 50 km of a coastline that are at high risk of entering the sea. Such waste is difficult to collect, often severely contaminated with salt, sand and other substances, and frequently consists of mixed colors and materials, making mechanical recycling extremely difficult.

Terracle's certification recognizes its ability to recycle these marine waste streams. The certificate identifies mixed OBP plastic waste as an input and chemical feedstocks such as terephthalic acid (TPA) and ethylene glycol (EG) as outputs under the Circular category. These materials are used in everyday products including apparel, beverage bottles and electronic components.

Approximately eight million tons of plastic enter the sea each year, threatening marine ecosystems and eventually reaching the human food chain as microplastics. Conventional mechanical recycling, often limited to clean clear PET bottles, struggles with colored or mixed plastics and can reduce material quality through repeated cycles.

Terracle's depolymerization technology addresses these structural limitations. Whereas polymerization combines raw materials to create plastics, depolymerization reverses the process—much like returning bread to flour and water. The company says chemical decomposition below 100°C makes molecular recovery possible regardless of color or contamination, yielding feedstocks with purity above 99%.

The quality approaches that of virgin petrochemical feedstocks. Terracle has produced high-purity recycled TPA at ton scale in Korea and, at the time of the report, expected its 4,000-ton-per-year hydrolysis depolymerization plant to begin operating in the first half of the year.

Government and international recognition has also grown. Terracle exhibited at Samsung's sustainability pavilion during CES 2024 in Las Vegas and was selected for Korea's Deep Tech Startup 1000+ Project. A ministerial visit to the company's demonstration facility at the Green Convergence Cluster highlighted its technology; the article also reports preliminary Green Unicorn recognition.
Terracle CEO Kwon Kibaek (right) at a preliminary Green Unicorn award ceremony

The technology is already being tested in practice. In March 2024 Terracle signed an MOU with the Busan office of the Korea Marine Environment Management Corporation and the Busan branch of the tugboat industry association. Those organizations collect marine waste in Busan Port, and Terracle converts it into chemical feedstocks.

CEO Kwon does not regard plastic itself as inherently bad. He notes that modern civilization depends on plastics and argues that the real problem is the lack of effective circularity. Rather than simply calling for reduced usage, he sees repeated recycling without environmental pollution as a more practical solution.

The company is also focusing on fashion. Around 60% of clothing globally is made from polyester. According to figures cited in the report, textile waste accounts for approximately 12% of municipal solid waste and fashion for around 10% of global carbon emissions, while only about 1% of discarded textiles is recycled. Mixed colors and materials make conventional recycling difficult.

Terracle says its depolymerization technology can recover raw materials from discarded clothing. Kwon said the technology could expand recycling across polyester textiles, banners and garments, and that the company would continue collaborating with the fashion sector.

As global brands in Europe and North America increase their use of recycled materials, demand for ISCC PLUS-certified high-purity feedstocks is rising. Recycled feedstocks from marine waste also carry meaningful environmental and product-story value. The OBP certification provides Terracle with a basis for participating in global sustainable materials supply chains.

Plastic that might have reached the sea can instead become clean feedstock and return as new products. Terracle's certification represents international recognition of the technical possibility of this full circularity cycle.
Online News Team

title: KGCCI Innovation Awards Recognize Dolbomdream, Terracle and Tround
summary: Terracle won second prize at the 11th KGCCI Innovation Awards.
Its Terra-X™ process for chemically recycling waste PET was recognized as a potential enabler of sustainable plastics circularity.
caption: 제11회 KGCCI 이노베이션 어워드 시상식 / 플래텀 제공

body.text: The Korean-German Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KGCCI) held the 11th KGCCI Innovation Awards at the Ambassador Seoul Pullman Hotel on the 20th. Dolbomdream won first prize, Terracle second prize and Tround third prize.

Supported by Korea's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and Ministry of SMEs and Startups, the awards recognize companies creating meaningful value in Korea through innovative ideas and business strategies. A Korean-German jury evaluates five criteria: level of innovation, market validation, business performance impact, social benefit, and diversity and inclusion.
Five finalists pitched at the ceremony, after which electronic voting on site determined the winners.

Dolbomdream developed Carely, described as the world's first non-invasive pneumatic ballistocardiography system. Air-pressure sensors embedded in cushions or clothing detect subtle chest movement and analyze heart and breathing patterns. AI algorithms aim to identify early signs of arrhythmia, sleep apnea and heart failure. Clinical verification was conducted with hospitals and research institutions.
Dolbomdream CEO Kim Jihoon said the company would continue developing Carely to help older adults live safely and independently through intelligent non-invasive monitoring.

Terracle presented Terra-X™, a chemical recycling process that depolymerizes waste PET into TPA and EG at low temperature and atmospheric pressure. The report states that it processes dyes and adhesives without separate pretreatment, achieves product purity above 99.9%, and reduces unit carbon emissions by approximately 50% compared with petroleum-based TPA.
Terracle project manager Lee Hyunmin said the company would continue technological innovation and business expansion to help build a sustainable plastics circularity system.

Tround developed the SoundXR Chair, designed to reproduce home-theater-scale spatial audio from a personal chair. A curved speaker frame approximately 30 cm from the user provides five or more channels of direct sound. The system translates movie and game audio data into vibration in the seat and backrest, combining audio and tactile experiences. An accredited test reportedly found a 16.78% improvement in immersion.
Tround CEO Park Jaebeom said the company was establishing a new category of sound chair through SoundXR.

KGCCI representative Marie-Antonia von Schönburg said innovation drives the economy and society forward and that this year's finalists demonstrated the possibilities created by combining creativity and collaboration.

title: Terracle Exhibits at Korea ESG Eco Expo's Circularity Pavilion
summary: Terracle is exhibiting at the plastics circularity solutions pavilion of Korea ESG Eco Expo.
It will introduce recycled materials produced with Terra-X hydrolysis depolymerization technology.
caption: 테라클, ‘대한민국 ESG 친환경대전’ 플라스틱 자원순환 솔루션 특별관 참가 / 필드뉴스

body.text: [Field News, reporter Lee Seungcheol] Terracle announced on the 22nd that it would participate in the Plastics Circularity Solutions Pavilion at Korea ESG Eco Expo, held September 24–26 at COEX in Seoul.
The exhibition will feature recycled terephthalic acid (Cr-TPA) and ethylene glycol (Cr-EG), produced using Terracle's Terra-X hydrolysis depolymerization technology.

While some depolymerization facilities using methanol or glycol are commercially operating overseas, hydrolysis depolymerization was described in the report as an emerging technology without established commercial cases.
Through the exhibition, Terracle plans to introduce its technologies and products to industry professionals and the public and explore new circularity partnerships.
Korea ESG Eco Expo is an ESG-focused exhibition hosted by Korea's Ministry of Environment and jointly organized by the Korea Environmental Industry & Technology Institute and Messe Esang.
The event presents sustainable solutions in carbon neutrality, circularity and energy efficiency. The accompanying Korea ESG Forum discusses ESG strategies and policy directions across industries.
Visitors could register in advance through the official website by the 23rd for free admission. Forum details were also available on the exhibition website.

title: Terracle Participates in Startup Mahakumbh 2025 in India
summary: Terracle aims to introduce depolymerization-based circularity technology as it considers a plant in India.
The company is exploring partnerships with recyclers and chemical companies in the Indian market.
caption: 이미지 제공 - 테라클

body.text: Terracle, led by CEO Kwon Kibaek, announced its participation in Startup Mahakumbh 2025, held April 3–5 in New Delhi, India.

Founded in 2021, Terracle develops chemical recycling technologies that return waste plastics and clothing to high-purity raw materials. Its work focuses on composite plastics, polyester textiles and films that are difficult to recycle mechanically and would otherwise be incinerated or landfilled. The process produces recycled terephthalic acid (cr-TPA) and ethylene glycol (cr-EG).
As these chemical feedstocks are widely used in PET, other polyester products and numerous industries, the company believes its circularity solutions can deliver significant industrial value.

At the exhibition, Terracle plans to introduce its low-temperature, atmospheric-pressure hydrolysis depolymerization technology, the waste streams it can process and the applications of cr-TPA and cr-EG.

The company previously operated a fully automated continuous depolymerization plant for 18 months, processing more than one ton per day to demonstrate scalability. Having started with two pilot plants, it was reportedly expanding toward a new facility with annual capacity of 4,000 tons, while seeking to meet strict global quality standards.

Terracle says its low-temperature, atmospheric-pressure process offers lower carbon emissions and improved energy efficiency relative to output, limiting environmental impact while allowing competitive recycled material pricing.

The company plans to use these advantages to pursue international cooperation and market entry. A representative said Terracle would explore joint technology development, licensing and localized partnerships to address waste problems in India and other regions, as well as new business opportunities with companies investing in ESG and circularity.

Its immediate priority is to establish a local recycling plant in India, addressing the country's plastic waste challenges and substantial TPA demand. Terracle plans to seek collaboration with local customers and companies in the recycling and chemical industries.

Startup Mahakumbh 2025, organized by the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce & Industry (FICCI), was the event's second edition. The previous year attracted about 48,000 visitors and over 1,300 exhibitors, including prominent Indian figures such as Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Under the theme 'BIGGER, BETTER, BOLDER,' organizers anticipated approximately 3,000 exhibitors and 50,000 visitors across 12 sectors including AI, cybersecurity, biotechnology, healthcare, agriculture and climate technology.

Korea's Ministry of SMEs and Startups and Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development supported the participation of 11 promising Korean startups. Selected through preparatory training, they showcased technologies and business models in the K-Startup Pavilion while meeting Indian investors and partners to explore market opportunities.

title: Terracle's Depolymerization Technology Advances ESG in Fashion
summary: Terracle applies depolymerization technology to the challenge of discarded textiles.
It turns colored and composite plastics and marine waste into raw materials including TPA and EG.
caption: 섬유폐기물 / 세계일보

body.text: The rise of ultra-fast fashion brands that move from design to sale in as little as one week has intensified concerns over discarded clothing. According to figures cited from the World Bank, textiles account for 12% of municipal solid waste worldwide, while fashion is responsible for around 10% of global carbon emissions.

Polyester accounts for roughly 60% of clothing worldwide and is chemically the same material as PET plastic. Different colors and mixed fibers make it difficult to recycle, with only about 1% of discarded textiles reportedly recovered. Landfilling and incineration cause serious environmental impacts. In response, the fashion industry faces increasing pressure to pursue ESG practices. The EU has been extending producer-responsibility recycling measures to textiles and moving toward mandatory separate collection of textile waste.

Despite sustainability initiatives, much of the fashion economy remains linear, with garments landfilled or incinerated. Chemical recycling company Terracle aims to help fashion brands establish circular ESG practices by converting difficult-to-recycle synthetic garments into their original feedstocks through depolymerization.

Terracle uses a catalytic system to depolymerize PET into monomers, an emerging technology that major companies worldwide are working to commercialize. The company says its process minimizes environmental impacts and energy use and can operate below 60°C at ambient pressure, unlike conventional methods requiring high heat and pressure.

By recovering terephthalic acid (TPA) and ethylene glycol (EG), the building blocks of polyester, depolymerization can extend recycling to discarded clothing as well as colored and composite plastics and marine waste that mechanical recycling has struggled to handle.

Terracle also supplies high-purity recycled feedstocks comparable to petroleum-derived TPA. These materials are used across packaging, textiles, films, engineering plastics, paints, adhesives and tire cords, offering wider applicability than conventional recycled PET chips.

CEO Kwon Kibaek expects depolymerization to expand recycling to polyester and polyurethane textiles, banners and clothing. He added that Terracle plans to develop recycling technologies for PU, nylon and other wastes while continuing circularity partnerships in fashion.
Terracle became the first company in Korea to produce high-purity recycled TPA at ton scale, and was selected for the Ministry of SMEs and Startups' Deep Tech Startup 1000+ Project.

title: Four Companies Including Terracle to Build Plants in Dangjin Under KRW 105.9 Billion Investment
summary: Dangjin signed an investment agreement totaling KRW 105.9 billion with four companies including Terracle.
Terracle plans to build a plant in the Hapdeok industrial complex based on environmentally responsible depolymerization.
caption: 11일 당진시가 충남도청 대회의실에서 ㈜비츠로셀, ㈜이노그린메탈, 신포메탈㈜, 테라클㈜와 산단 내 생산공장 신·증설 투자 협약을 맺은 후 관계자들이 협약서를 들고 기념 촬영을 하고 있다. / 당진시 제공

body.text: Dangjin City in Chungcheongnam-do signed investment agreements totaling KRW 105.9 billion with four companies.

On the 11th, the city announced that Governor Kim Taeheum, Mayor Oh Seonghwan and company representatives attended a signing ceremony at the provincial government office for new and expanded plants within industrial complexes. The four companies are Vitzrocell, Inno Green Metal, Shinpo Metal and Terracle.
Vitzrocell, a lithium battery manufacturer based in Hapdeok Induspark, plans to expand its lithium secondary battery production plant on a 17,334-square-meter site.

Inno Green Metal, which specializes in recycling strategic metals such as vanadium and molybdenum, will establish a production facility on 15,687 square meters in the Seokmun National Industrial Complex.
Shinpo Metal will build an aluminum billet plant for aluminum rolling products on 8,422 square meters in the Seokmun National Industrial Complex.

Terracle, which produces terephthalic acid and ethylene glycol from PET using environmentally responsible depolymerization technology, will build its plant on a 7,000-square-meter site in Hapdeok General Industrial Complex.
The city expected construction to begin as early as the second half of that year, with total investment of KRW 105.9 billion.
The Chungnam Institute estimated short-term economic effects of KRW 150.7 billion in induced production, KRW 53.5 billion in added value and about 533 jobs arising from the investment.
After completion, the plants were projected to create around 130 permanent jobs and generate approximately KRW 208.3 billion in annual production effects and KRW 34.3 billion in added value.
The agreement encourages the use of locally sourced materials and priority hiring of local talent, which is expected to stimulate the provincial economy.
Mayor Oh said the efforts to create a business-friendly Dangjin were bearing fruit and pledged to continue attracting quality investment that benefits the local economy.

title: Terracle: Enabling Plastics to Be Used Indefinitely Without Pollution
summary: Terracle develops chemical recycling technology that turns waste plastics back into TPA and EG.
The company is growing as a sustainable ESG solutions provider following a Series A fundraising round.
caption: [2024 인천강소연구개발특구 기업 CEO] 플라스틱을 환경오염 없이 무한하게 사용하도록 하는 기업 ‘테라클’ / 한경잡앤조이

body.text: 'Terracle believes plastics are among the most convenient materials humanity has created. Global plastics production has never declined in human history, and replacing plastics entirely is currently unrealistic. Beyond convenience, plastics serve hygiene, safety, economic and environmental needs across fashion, automotive, food, healthcare, electronics and many other industries. Our vision is to enable plastics to be used indefinitely without pollution.'

Terracle is a chemical recycling company founded in July 2021 by CEO Kwon Kibaek. It conducts R&D to expand its technology from household waste to difficult-to-recycle industrial waste, marine waste and discarded home appliances.

The company primarily recycles colored and composite plastic waste that is hard to process mechanically, producing recycled monomers CR-TPA and CR-EG. For customers, it offers solutions supporting zero industrial waste, lower waste treatment costs, ESG, greenhouse-gas reductions, closed loops and recycled feedstock supply.

Engineering team leader Yoo Minhyung said Terracle's depolymerization recovers approximately 97–99% of feedstocks from waste under Korea's Green Technology Certification criteria. He highlighted operation below 100°C without pressure, replacement of chemical solvents with waste where feasible and recovery of wastewater to minimize environmental impacts.

Based on that technology, Terracle can supply CR-TPA and CR-EG with purities above 99% at scale, allowing their use without additional additives or equipment expansion. TPA is widely applied to packaging, textiles, films, engineering plastics, paints, adhesives and tire cords and has broader applications than ordinary recycled PET chips.

'Many sales opportunities began with customers approaching us first. We have actively used open innovation and partnership programs to develop the market. Going forward we intend to approach overseas consumer goods companies in fashion, food and beverages seeking circularity solutions.'

The company emphasizes offering competitive products through technology before promoting environmental virtue. It regards collaboration with customers and industry to build a circular economy as especially important.
Terracle completed a KRW 10.5 billion Series A funding round with Envisioning Partners, DSC Investment, Hyundai Motor Group's ZER01NE, Korea Development Bank and Schmidt.
At the time of the article, Terracle had 17 employees, including 13 in R&D, organized into research, engineering, quality control and production teams. It aimed to grow to 30 employees that year.

Yoo said compensation and rewards were determined by performance and peer evaluations rather than age, career history or seniority, and described the culture as having few unnecessary meetings, fast decisions and frequent communication.

CEO Kwon said he wanted a workplace where team members could grow their abilities and gain recognition and rewards for results. To him, a dream workplace means challenging personal limits and continuing to grow, not simply having easy work or work-life balance.

Terracle was located in the Incheon Strong R&D Special Zone, a Korean program that designates compact, dense areas around universities and government research institutes to promote commercialization of public technology. Companies in the zone may access commercialization funding, infrastructure, tax benefits and regulatory support.

title: 97% Recovery from Hard-to-Recycle Plastics at 99% Purity Draws Major Corporate Interest
summary: News Today interviewed Terracle CEO Kwon Kibaek about depolymerization and business strategy.
Terracle is building a sustainable plastics circularity system by recovering original raw materials from waste plastics.
caption: 테라클(주) 권기백 대표 / 테라클(주) 제공

body.text: [부산 / 뉴스투데이=심지훈·윤나라 기자] 지난 2019년부터 올해 6회째를 맞이한 부산의 대표 창업투자경진대회인 ‘B-스타트업 챌린지’가 오는 6월 19일 부산 e스포츠경기장에서 개최된다. <뉴스투데이>에서 지난 2021년 3회 대회에서 은상을 수상한 테라클(주)의 권기백 대표를 만나 친환경 제품, 수상의 배경과 성과 등에 대한 인터뷰를 진행했다.
다음은 권기백 대표와의 일문일답.
Q. 테라클의 연혁과 기술에 대해 간단한 설명 부탁드립니다.
아직 3년이 되지 않은 초기 스타트업이고, 지금 17명 정도로 구성되어 있습니다. 저희가 하고 있는 일은 해중합 기술을 사용해서 폐플라스틱을 원재료로 되돌리고, 그 원재료를 판매하는 일을 하고 있습니다.

해중합 기술에 대해 조금 더 설명 드리면, PET(폴리에스테르)를 위주로 재활용하는데, 우리가 알고 있는 PET는 패키지류가 대부분이지만 사실 제가 입고 있는 옷도 PET 100%고요, PET를 길게 실처럼 뽑으면 섬유가 됩니다. PET는 TPA라는 백색 분말과 에틸렌글리콜이라는 투명 액체를 합쳐서 만드는데, 그걸 중합이라고 표현하고 이것을 해체하는 게 해중합입니다.
물리적 재활용이 폐플라스틱을 잘게 부수고 다시 뭉쳐 제품을 만드는 방식이라면, 테라클은 PET를 원료인 TPA(테레프탈산)와 EG(에틸렌글리콜)로 되돌려 판매하는 일을 하고 있습니다. 업계에서는 2021년도부터 본격적으로 알려져 차세대 재활용 기술이라고 표현하며 주요 대기업과 글로벌 기업들도 이 기술을 상용화하기 위해 연구개발을 하고 있습니다.
Q. 어떻게 이런 기술을 실현시킬 수 있었는지 궁금합니다.
해중합 기술은 유래가 30년은 족히 넘은 기술입니다. 원래 있던 개념이고 화학 관련 학과에서도 간단하게 배우는 개념이나, 환경적·경제적 이유로 상용화에 아무도 도전하는 사람이 없었던 기술이었습니다. 저는 단지 해결하고 싶은 문제가 있었고, 문제를 해결할 기술을 찾았고, 함께할 팀을 꾸려 ‘테라클’이라는 이름으로 도전하는 것뿐입니다.

이 사업을 하기 전 광고 회사를 다녔습니다. 당시 특정 음료의 용기를 재활용한다는 내용의 광고가 있었는데, 그 음료의 용기는 실질적으로 재활용이 어려운 품목이었습니다. 그때부터 근본적인 문제를 해결해보겠다고 마음먹었고, 카이스트 오픈벤처랩 프로그램을 시작했습니다. 이후 교수님 자문을 받으며 정부출연기관과 대학의 기술들을 찾아다녔고, 근본적인 문제를 해결할 수 있는 기술이 해중합이라고 생각했습니다.
Q. 2021년 창업투자경진대회 수상 배경에 대해 말씀해주세요.
수상은 사실 우수상이 아니라 은상이었습니다. 은상은 5000만 원 투자를 받을 수 있었어요. 대회 당시에는 사업자등록증도 없었고 저만 유일하게 예비 창업자였습니다. 보통 이런 대회는 예비창업자 부문과 기창업자 부문이 나뉘어서 진행되는데, 그렇지 않음에도 아이디어가 좋으면 기회를 주는 점이 좋은 것 같습니다.
Q. 회사가 급성장하고 있는 것 같은데, 어떻습니까?
저희는 빠르게 성장하고 있습니다. 지속적으로 신규 채용을 늘리고 있고 공장도 새로운 증설을 준비하고 있습니다. 현재 고객들의 수요를 맞춰야 해서 빠르게 커야만 하는 상황이라 그것 외에는 부담스럽지는 않습니다.
Q. 환경에 대한 기여도가 굉장히 있는 것 같습니다.
화학적 재활용에는 “재활용을 할 때 더 환경오염이 되는 것 아니냐”라는 이슈가 있습니다. 저희는 모든 공정이 100도 이하에서 운전되고, 화학 용매나 촉매 같은 것들은 재사용하고 있습니다. 공정에서 사용되는 물까지 최대한 재사용합니다. 본격적으로 대량 양산을 계획하고 있는데, 저희가 예상하는 환경적·산업적 파급력은 굉장할 것이라 기대합니다.
폐기물 수급 과정 / 테라클(주) 제공
Q. 녹색 기술 인증도 받으셨네요.
환경부에서 나오는 인증인데요, 이 인증은 일반 소비자에게 판매를 하지 않다보니 큰 필요는 없습니다. 그래도 저희가 인증을 받은 건, 이 공정이 친환경적인 공정이라는 것을 가시적으로 인증받으면 좋겠다는 생각이었습니다.

해당 인증을 받는 데는 환경부의 명확한 기준이 있습니다. 쉽게 말하면 폐기물이 95% 전환되어야 하는데, 저희는 97%가 나왔습니다. 평가도 서면으로만 하는 것이 아니라 심사위원이 회사로 와서 처음부터 끝까지 다 봅니다. 낮은 온도로 운전하고 에너지 사용량이 적은 것을 보여드렸고, 플라스틱 화학 분해에 의한 모노머 제조 기술 항목에서 폐플라스틱 재활용으로 최초 인증을 받았습니다.
Q. 테라클 원료의 가격 경쟁력은 어느 정도인지?
저희는 직접 재생 PET를 만드는 것이 아니라 PET를 활용하는 고객들에게 PET의 원료만 판매합니다. 석유화학 제품보다는 비싸지만, 지금처럼 적은 양을 생산하는 상황에서도 해외 유사 제품의 반값이라는 점이 핵심입니다. 앞으로 규모의 경제가 실현되면서 가격은 계속 낮아질 예정입니다.

또한 재활용이 어려운 폐기물을 재활용한다는 점은 단순히 재생 테레프탈산과 재생 에틸렌글리콜의 가격 경쟁력을 넘어서, 고객의 ESG, 폐기물 처리비용 감소, closed loop, 탄소감축과 같은 다양한 이점으로 이어집니다. 고객 입장에서도 조금 비싸더라도 고부가가치 제품에 안정적으로 적용할 수 있고, 대규모 양산라인에도 적용 가능해 찾아주시는 것 같습니다.
Q. 주요 고객사는? 대기업들만 가능한 것인지.
산업 구조적으로 워낙 큰 설비와 축적된 기술이 필요하기 때문에, 아쉽지만 저희 소재는 대기업, 중견기업 말고는 쓰지 않습니다. 워낙 대형 산업이라 저희가 생산하는 몇 백 톤 단위의 제품들은 고객사에서 하루면 전부 소진하는 아주 작은 양입니다. 때문에 수요를 맞추기 위해 빠르게 증설하고 있습니다.
Q. 공장 이전 계획이 있으신지.
당초 계획은 부산 강서구에 더 큰 공장 증설을 계획하고 있었고 지금도 최선을 다하고 있지만, 입주가 가능한 부지와 물건이 없는 상태입니다. 이번에 저희 업종코드가 환경부의 규제 샌드박스를 통해 폐기물 처리업이 아니라 다른 코드를 받았음에도 산단이나 지자체에서 유선으로 거부하는 경우가 있어 지금은 지역 구분 없이 전국의 매물을 보고 있습니다.
Q. 부산에 공장이 생긴다면 일자리 창출 효과를 기대할 수 있겠습니다.
저희는 기본적으로 자동화 공정이고 앞으로도 공정 부분마다 연구할 것들이 많아 단순 노동 인력도 채용하지만 연구 인력이 많이 필요합니다. 테라클에는 부산 소재 대학 출신들이 많은데, 부산에는 화학이나 친환경 관련 기업이 별로 없습니다. 부산에 화학과 자원순환, 친환경 소재 관련 양질의 일자리가 생긴다면 부산 청년 구직자들에게도 좋은 기회가 될 것 같습니다.
실험 중인 테라클 연구원 / 테라클(주) 제공
Q. 부산항 해양 폐기물 재활용을 위해 한국해양공단 부산지사와 업무 협약을 했다는데.
저희 고객사 중 한 곳이 해양공단을 소개해주셨습니다. 해양공단은 해양 폐기물을 수거하는 역할을 하는데, 문제는 수거를 해도 태우는 방법 외에 특별한 재활용 방법이 없다는 점입니다. 공단에서도 다양한 방법을 찾아다녔지만, 염분과 이물질이 많이 포함돼 물리적 재활용으로 활용이 어렵다고 들었습니다.
저희가 수급한 폐기물은 폐그물이나 폐로프, 해양 폐플라스틱 등이 있었는데, 저희 기술로 세척 없이 염분과 이물질 제거가 가능해서 재활용이 가능합니다. 앞으로 전국의 해양 폐기물을 재활용할 수 있도록 노력하고자 하며, 한국해양공단 부산지사와도 긴밀한 협업을 통해 해양 환경을 지킬 수 있도록 노력하고자 합니다.
Q. 앞으로의 계획이나 꿈이 있다면?
테라클은 인류가 만들어낸 가장 편리한 물질이 플라스틱이라고 생각합니다. 지금까지 인류 역사상 한 번도 플라스틱 생산량이 줄어든 적이 없고, 현실적으로 지금은 대체하기가 힘듭니다. 위생이나 의료, 패션, 자동차, 전자제품 등 거의 모든 업계가 다양한 형태의 플라스틱을 필요로 하기 때문입니다.
그래서 테라클의 목표는 플라스틱을 환경오염 없이 무한하게 사용하는 것입니다. 그 핵심은 기술입니다. 친환경이나 좋은 일을 먼저 내세우기보다는 기술을 통해 경쟁력 있는 제품을 선보이고, 고객들과 산업계가 함께 자원순환 사회를 구축할 수 있도록 하는 것이 가장 중요하다고 생각합니다.
회사 내부적으로는 구성원들이 자기의 능력을 충분히 성장시키며, 누구나 성과를 내고 충분한 보상을 얻는 환경을 만들고 싶습니다. 워라밸이나 쉬운 업무가 아니라 각자의 한계에 도전하고 계속 성장하며, 성공을 통해 인류에 기여하고 싶은 사람들이 모이는 곳이면 좋겠습니다.
